issues.legal_issue: Land used for open-cast mining operations, or land adjacent to a mine used for the mine’s purposes, falls within the statutory definition of a mine.
material_facts: The disputed land formed the surface above a coal seam and was used for mining operations involving the seam below it.
The evidence showed open-cast mining in the area.
The disputed land was adjacent to a coal mine and was used for stacking coal and making local sales.
issues.conclusion: The disputed land was a mine within the meaning of the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(h) of the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973 defines a mine to include an excavation where operations to search for or obtain minerals are carried on; clause (iv) includes open-cast workings, and clause (vi) includes land adjacent to a mine and used for its purposes. The surface used for mining operations is part of the mine because excavation cannot be carried on without it.

predicates.civil_title_dispute: A civil proceeding concerns a claimant’s asserted title to land in a mining area.
predicates.surface_used_for_mining_operations: The land’s surface is used in carrying on mining operations.
predicates.land_adjacent_to_mine: The land lies next to a mine.
predicates.land_used_for_mine_purposes: The land is used for purposes of the mine, such as storing or selling its coal.

issues.definition: When a civil title dispute concerns land whose surface is used for mining or land next to a mine that serves the mine’s purposes, the land falls within the mine definition.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant’s title to land forming part of an acquired coal mine is extinguished when the rights in that mine vest absolutely in the government free from encumbrances.
material_facts: The claimants asserted title to leasehold land under a registered lease and sought a declaration of their rights and confirmation of possession.
The disputed land was found to form part of a mine within the meaning of the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973.
The rights in the coal mine vested in the Central Government free from encumbrances, and the Act provided for vesting those rights in a government company.
issues.conclusion: The claimants’ title, if any, to the disputed land stood extinguished upon vesting of the mine’s rights under the Act; it was immaterial whether the mine had belonged to the State or to private parties.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973 transfers and vests absolutely in the Central Government the owners’ rights, title and interest in the specified coal mines, free from encumbrances. Sections 5 and 6 address vesting in a government company and the discharge of encumbrances upon vesting. State of West Bengal v. Union of India, [1964] 1 SCR 371, was relied on for Parliament’s competence to legislate for acquisition of property owned by a State.

predicates.civil_title_claim: A claimant seeks recognition of title to land in a civil proceeding.
predicates.land_fell_within_acquired_coal_mine: The land was found to form part of a coal mine covered by the acquisition.
predicates.mine_rights_vested_in_government_free_of: The rights in the coal mine vested in the government without being subject to encumbrances.

issues.definition: When a civil title claim concerns land forming part of an acquired coal mine and the mine’s rights vest in government free of encumbrances, the claimant’s title is extinguished.

issues.legal_issue: A party that understood the factual issue at trial and chose to adduce evidence on it cannot later prevent the court from considering that evidence merely because the issue was not properly pleaded or framed.
material_facts: The parties went to trial understanding that the location and use of the disputed land were in issue.
Both sides chose to adduce evidence concerning those matters.
The courts below considered that evidence.
On appeal, the claimants argued that the evidence should not be considered because there was no proper pleading or issue for determination.
issues.conclusion: The claimants could not retract from the evidence or prevent its consideration, and the Court rejected their contention.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle stated in Kunju Kesavan v. M.M. Philip & Others, [1964] 3 SCR 634: where the parties understood the central factual matter and tried the case on that basis, the absence of a formally framed issue does not prevent the evidence from being considered.

rule.if: civil_appeal and parties_understood_factual_issue and parties_chose_to_adduce_evidence_on_it and lower_courts_considered_that_evidence

predicates.civil_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a civil case.
predicates.parties_understood_factual_issue: The parties understood the factual matter they were required to prove at trial.
predicates.parties_chose_to_adduce_evidence_on_it: The parties voluntarily presented evidence concerning that factual matter.
predicates.lower_courts_considered_that_evidence: The lower courts considered the evidence presented on that factual matter.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal, when the parties understood a factual issue, chose to present evidence on it, and the lower courts considered that evidence, a party cannot prevent its consideration.
